rows.what the ink shows: At the deleted line start, a dense upright mass with a right-sloping spur is followed by a low squared joining stroke and a small terminal loop. Heavy overwriting prevents separating an initial c and the proposed a/r sequence even at 8×.

After the comma, two small open/looped forms survive at the left, followed by a long double horizontal cancellation. A dot above the middle and several low descending remnants remain, but the deletion hides the letter boundaries needed to establish ceci implique.

Own targeted reinspection confirms a compact abbreviation rather than a separately written En effet: a short initial downstroke and horizontal bar join a tall hooked f-like stem with a lower loop. Overlap makes the count of f strokes uncertain, hence Ef or Eff. The separate period is already outside this mark in the source and is not duplicated in the reading.

Immediately after K there is a separate short hooked s, a low connected middle, and a final angled t, supporting sont rather than the initial e of est. The following long ouvert- group has a terminal loop/tail, then a separate angular et and the tall initial f of fermées with a final detached low ending.

Between et and dans are exactly two separate heavy, nearly horizontal parallel strokes, with no connecting curve, e loop, s, or upright terminal t. This is an equals sign rather than the written word est.

Own targeted reinspection confirms a secure closing parenthesis and the preceding K-shaped upright with right arm, preceded by an opening curved stroke. The initial large curved character is overwritten by radiating horizontal/diagonal strokes; these permit C or E but do not distinguish them. The surviving (K) is therefore transcribed, with uncertainty confined to the initial C/E.

The deleted word begins with an open c, followed by repeated low angular humps; two taller strokes occur centrally, one visibly crossed, and a long low final joining stroke ends in a small curl. The visible c–hump sequence and crossed t support commutative beneath the deletion.

The abbreviation begins with a tall f stroke and a very long lower loop; its return rises into a shorter b/l group with a low curled joining stroke. A separate short upright crossed to the right forms the final t. These are abbreviated letters, not the expanded word faiblement.

The underlined letter after où is a small open curve with upper and lower rightward ends and a clear gap on the right; it has no closing right downstroke. The underlined a later at the end of the next line has a closed triangular body, unlike this open c.

The small insertion above trace T starts with a compact s-shaped sign, followed directly by a tall looped f and a low connected run with two separate i dots; the terminal e is a short hooked stroke. There is no extended semi- sequence or hyphen.

The targeted own enlargement shows a shallow initial cup followed by a flattened horizontal run, then a narrow descending f-loop and an immediately adjacent raised t-stroke. No separate orm sequence is visible between the f-loop and raised t. The shorter abbreviation unift is plausible, but the flattened prefix and compressed run do not warrant a fully certain expansion or contraction.

The baseline glyph has a long descending stem and angular loop crossed by a heavy oblique and horizontal cancellation. Its original mu/rho distinction is lost in the crossing. A separate elevated replacement has two low open bends followed by a rightward stroke and short terminal down-hook, with no rho bowl or long descender: the replacement reads mu. Both cancelled and inserted levels are retained.

After pour, a high initial stem descends into a narrow loop below the line, then returns to a shoulder extending up and right before hooking down. A full right-hand oval is not closed, but this long lower return can support competing cursive mu/rho readings.

Immediately after d in the integral, the connected symbol descends diagonally into a long narrow lower return, rises to a pointed right shoulder and ends with a short downward hook. The attachment to d obscures the left entry; the open shoulder alone does not securely distinguish cursive mu from rho.

The targeted own enlargement shows the small symbol between supp and the equals sign as an open angular left cusp continuing into a low horizontal arm. The space below is present and contains no descending stem; the symbol has no closed rho bowl. This compressed open form supports mu, though its tiny size keeps confidence medium.

notes: Initial primary report saved before independent review. M0356 compact glyph and M0359 overwritten expression need an independent reading; M0358 equals-sign recovery is clear but substantial enough to request independent confirmation. M0354 and M0355 remain obscured by cancellation after targeted enlargement. Only M0354–M0361 were adjudicated. No Hua comparison or OCR was used.

Initial primary report is preserved at deliverable/audit/revisions/scan022_a_initial.json. After independent review, own reinspection narrowed M0356 to Ef/Eff and M0359 to C/E followed by secure (K); both remain undecided with low confidence. M0358 remains $=$ without an additional primary view. Independent review reports were not altered or incorporated as primary viewing time.

notes.notes: Primary report after one authorized targeted reconciliation of M0364/M0365/M0368. M0364 retains uncertain unift|uniformt rather than expanding the abbreviation; M0365 preserves the crossed uncertain glyph and separately inserted mu; M0368 reads mu at medium confidence. M0366/M0367 remain unchanged and were not inspected again. Initial primary timing and original report preserved separately; independent peer timing/views are not incorporated as own evidence. No OCR, external transcription, source edits, or later page inspection.
